children: jumped 7.4% Monday after investor Michael Burry disclosed that he bought common and preferred shares of the building-products company, citing its consolidation strategy and depressed stock price.
Burry, who became widely known for betting against the U.S. housing market before the 2008 financial crisis and was portrayed in “The Big Short,” disclosed the investment in a Substack post.
“QXO is a building products roll-up. Scale makes sense in this business,” Burry wrote.
He said QXO’s economics should improve as the company expands through acquisitions. Burry also pointed to Chief Executive Brad Jacobs’ track record of building companies through consolidation.
“The stock is way down, and I see an opportunity to jump on board,” Burry wrote.

QXO has pursued an aggressive acquisition strategy in the fragmented building-products distribution market. The company completed its acquisition of Beacon Roofing Supply in 2025, giving it a large distribution network serving roofing and other construction markets.

For investors, Burry’s purchase adds a prominent value investor to QXO’s shareholder base, but his thesis depends partly on management successfully executing additional acquisitions and extracting benefits from greater scale. The company also remains exposed to construction and remodeling demand, making the pace of any housing-market recovery important to its results.

title: QXO jumps after ‘Big Short’ investor Michael Burry reveals stake
